questions.q: Per this lesson, what is technical debt, precisely?
options: Accumulated shortcuts and compromises, made for understandable reasons, that make future changes harder and riskier than they should be
Any feature on the platform that is older than two years
A feature that no end users currently use
Any customization built by a developer who has since left the company
questions.explain: Technical debt isn't just age or lack of usage — it's specifically the accumulated cost of past shortcuts on future changes.

questions.q: Why does a hard-coded sys_id in a Business Rule count as technical debt?
options: It was a quick fix taken under deadline pressure that can silently break when that record's sys_id differs across environments
Hard-coded values always cause an immediate production outage
It is explicitly disallowed by ServiceNow platform rules
It has no real risk since sys_ids never change between environments
questions.explain: The shortcut works until an environment-specific sys_id difference causes it to silently fail — a classic deadline-driven debt pattern.

questions.q: What does this lesson say is the architect-level responsibility regarding technical debt?
options: Proactively identifying debt before it causes an incident, rather than waiting for a crisis to reveal it
Documenting debt only after it causes a production outage
Assigning debt remediation exclusively to the original developer who created it
Avoiding any audit of deprecated API usage until the next platform upgrade
questions.explain: Proactive, ongoing auditing is the architect's job — waiting until a crisis means the fix happens under the worst possible, unplanned conditions.

questions.q: What is the real, recurring organizational tension this lesson describes around technical debt?
options: Prioritizing debt remediation against constant pressure to ship new features, when stakeholders don't always see the risk of deferring the fix
Whether technical debt exists on ServiceNow instances at all
Deciding which single developer is responsible for all debt on the platform
Choosing between fixing debt and performing platform upgrades, as if they were mutually exclusive
questions.explain: The lesson frames this as an ongoing tension, not a one-time technical fix — every sprint competes new feature requests against debt remediation time.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say "this is blocking the feature stakeholders actually want" is often the strongest argument for debt remediation?
options: It reframes remediation as removing an obstacle to something the organization already wants, rather than as a competing priority against it
It is the only argument ServiceNow officially recognizes for prioritizing work
It guarantees the fix will take less time than any other justification
It avoids needing to document what the debt is currently costing
questions.explain: Framing debt as the blocker to a wanted feature turns the remediation case from "competing priority" into "prerequisite," which is a much easier case to defend.
